text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with two changed-quantity, two reordered and two moved-negation quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: The Kestrel Valley Cash for Food programme reached 4,200 households between March 2022 and September 2023, slightly above the original target of 4,000. Monthly transfers of 35 dollars were delivered through mobile wallets in eleven villages. Household food consumption scores improved for 68 percent of recipients, and the share of families reporting skipped meals fell from 41 percent to 19 percent. Transfers in upland villages were not delayed, but those near the river crossing were. Women-headed households spent a larger share of transfers on school fees than on food. Market traders were not consistently paid on time, and two vendors withdrew from the scheme in the final quarter. The team recommends indexing transfer values to local prices before the second phase begins.

passages.source_passage: Mbeyani District, in the Lower Ruvara region, has a population of roughly 310,000 people spread across 58 villages, many more than two hours' walk from the nearest health centre. Since 2019, the Ruvara Health Collective has trained 240 community health workers to provide home visits, malaria testing and referrals. Last year these workers conducted nearly 36,000 household visits. Most referrals were for childhood pneumonia rather than malaria. Villages with an active worker reported fewer under-five deaths and more facility births than villages without one. Supervision has been uneven: workers in the hill zones were not visited by supervisors each quarter, while those in the lowland zones were. Stock-outs of rapid test kits occurred in 17 percent of reporting months. The proposed project is not a parallel service but an extension of the existing district referral system.

passages.source_passage: At mid-term, the Talamo Farmer Field School Network had established 46 schools across three districts, enrolling 1,150 farmers, of whom 62 percent were women. Participants tested intercropping, mulching and improved seed on shared demonstration plots. Average sorghum yields on participants' own fields rose by about a third compared with the 2021 baseline. Farmers near the Saba road adopted mulching quickly, while farmers in the eastern hills favoured intercropping. Groups that kept written plot records outperformed those that relied on memory. Facilitators in Kiwa district were not paid stipends on time, but facilitators in Dorre district were. Attendance dropped below half during the October harvest weeks. Schools led by women facilitators were not among the weakest groups; several were among the strongest.

passages.source_passage: Board members, this update covers the Lantern Evening Literacy Circles from January to June 2024. We now run 28 evening classes in nine towns, up from 21 classes last year. Enrolment stands at 512 adults, and 74 percent of learners who sat the spring reading assessment reached the target level. Retention has improved, though classes in Harrow Bend did not keep their volunteer tutors, while classes in Millford did. Learners told us they valued reading medicine labels more than reading newspapers. The numeracy module is funded, but the tutor travel budget is not, and no new venues will open until autumn. The finance committee recommends that the board approve a modest reserve of 6,000 pounds for tutor travel.

passages.source_passage: Volunteers, this section explains how the midday meal works at the 14 primary schools supported by the Sunkari Nutrition Partnership in Bawa district. Each school serves a hot meal of millet porridge and beans to around 300 pupils by 12:30. Volunteers may help cooks with portioning, but they should not handle the cooking fires. Do not serve food that has stood for more than two hours. Pupils who have washed their hands may queue; those who have not must wait at the tap. Pupils in class one eat first and pupils in class six eat last, so younger children are not left waiting. Record meals in the green register, not in the blue attendance book. Last term, 8 percent of meal days were lost to late grain deliveries.

passages.source_passage: The Willowmere Community Counselling Service has delivered group and individual sessions in four neighbourhoods since its launch in April 2022. By the mid-term point, 860 clients had completed at least one session, and 57 percent completed the full eight-session cycle. Average distress scores on the screening tool fell by 9 points among those who finished. Clients referred by schools stayed longer than clients referred by clinics. Lay counsellors received monthly supervision, but they did not receive refresher training after the first year. Male clients did not drop out more often than female clients, but younger clients did. The service has not established a formal pathway to psychiatric care, which leaves severe cases dependent on informal referrals.

passages.source_passage: Between July 2022 and December 2023, the Harbourlight Family Tracing Project registered 212 separated children in the Velmora Plains camps. Caseworkers traced families for 131 of them, a reunification rate of 62 percent. Tracing teams prioritised unaccompanied infants over adolescents with siblings. Foster placements were used while tracing continued, and most children spent fewer than six months in foster care. Siblings were not separated in foster placements, although some were separated during tracing. Children placed with relatives settled faster than children placed with unrelated carers. Foster carers in the northern camp were not given a monthly allowance, but carers in the southern camp were. No child was returned to a household without a documented risk assessment.

variants.moved_negation_2: Siblings were separated in foster placements, although some were not separated during tracing.

passages.source_passage: This guide prepares volunteers to support the Dry Ridge Seeds for Resilience project in Kasembo county. Over the 2024 season, the project will distribute drought-tolerant cowpea and pearl millet seed to 1,800 households. Each household receives a 5-kilogram seed pack and a planting calendar. Explain to farmers that cowpea should be planted before the first rains and millet after them. Do not promise a particular yield; rainfall in the county has fallen by around 15 percent over two decades. Farmers who have saved their own seed may join the trial plots; farmers who have not should start with the project pack. Farmers should not burn crop residue, but they should leave it as mulch. Seed banks will be run by women's groups, and trial plots by youth groups.

passages.source_passage: In its second year, the Nirmala Valley Mother and Newborn Outreach Project, run by the Sahyog Health Trust, supported 6 rural clinics and 38 outreach sites. Community health visitors registered 2,950 pregnant women, and 81 percent attended at least four antenatal check-ups, compared with 64 percent in 2022. Most referrals came from midwives rather than village volunteers. Women in the hill blocks did not attend postnatal visits regularly, but women in the plains blocks did. Newborns were weighed at home, and mothers were counselled at the clinic. Ambulance response times improved to an average of 47 minutes. Families paid for routine transport but not for emergency referrals, and no clinic reported an oxytocin stock-out this year. We thank the Foundation for its continued support.

passages.source_passage: This board update summarises the Fairway Paralegal Outreach Service for the third quarter of 2024. Our 19 community paralegals held 140 legal awareness sessions and opened 386 new cases, mostly on land disputes rather than unpaid wages. About 45 percent of cases were resolved through mediation without going to court. Paralegals in Brenna county did not receive their new case-management tablets, while those in Tellan county did. Clients more often sought help with inheritance than with domestic violence, which surprised the team. We have renewed the agreement with the Brenna magistrates' office but not with the Tellan office. The board is asked to approve recruitment of two additional paralegals before December.
